question: What is the correct substitution for the word ‘screw’ in the idiom ‘Hit the screw on the head’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Nail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct and standard idiom is "Hit the nail on the head", which means to say or do exactly the right thing; to describe precisely the cause of a problem or the truth of a situation. (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना / ठीक निशाने पर बात करना)

◦ Example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the project failed because of poor planning.

• The given form "Hit the screw on the head" is a distorted version, so "screw" must be replaced by "nail".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bolt" is used in idioms like "a bolt from the blue" (a complete surprise) and "bolt upright".

• Option 2 "Crew" simply means a team of workers and forms no such idiom.

• Option 4 "Tack" appears in "get down to brass tacks" (to discuss the basic facts), not in this idiom.

NOTE

• Idioms of being exactly right: "hit the nail on the head", "spot on", "hit the bull's eye", "right on the money". Idioms must be memorised in their fixed form — a single changed word makes them wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

She prepares an unique dish in the cooking competition and won it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prepared a unique.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two errors must be corrected together in the underlined segment "prepares an unique":

◦ Tense: the second verb of the sentence is "won" (past tense), so the first verb must also be in the past tense — "prepared", not "prepares". Verbs joined by "and" must be parallel in tense.

◦ Article: the article before a word depends on its sound, not its spelling. "Unique" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yoo-neek"), so it takes "a", not "an" — "a unique dish".

• Hence the corrected sentence is: She prepared a unique dish in the cooking competition and won it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "prepares a unique" fixes the article but leaves the wrong present tense against "won".

• Option 2 "prepared an unique" fixes the tense but keeps the wrong article "an".

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because the segment has two clear errors.

NOTE

• Rule for A/AN: use "a" before a consonant sound — a university, a union, a European, a one-rupee note, a useful book. Use "an" before a vowel sound — an hour, an honest man, an MP, an umbrella.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Mosquito means small fly. It has a transmitter segmented body and a _________________ of wings. Male mosquitoes mainly feed on plant ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pair; nectar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 1 — Wings occur in twos, and the fixed collocation for two matching things worn/used together is "a pair of" — a pair of wings, a pair of shoes, a pair of scissors. (एक जोड़ी)

• Blank 2 — Male mosquitoes do not suck blood; they feed on "nectar", the sweet sugary liquid produced by flowers. (फूलों का रस / मकरंद)

◦ Correct: It has a transmitter segmented body and a pair of wings. Male mosquitoes mainly feed on plant nectar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "kind of wings" and "plant drink" are unidiomatic.

• Option 2 "set of wings" is possible only loosely, but "plant beverage" is not an expression in English.

• Option 4 "couple of wings" is informal and wrong here, and "liquor" means alcoholic drink — completely unsuitable.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: a pair of wings/gloves/trousers; a flock of birds; a swarm of bees/mosquitoes; a herd of cattle. Static point: only female mosquitoes (e.g., *Anopheles*, *Aedes*) bite humans, as they need blood protein for their eggs.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He had always wanted to work for himself; so, last year he _________ his job at the bank and is now running a tool business.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. left.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Left" (past tense of *leave*) means quit / resigned from / went away from. Since he wanted to work for himself and now runs his own business, he must have left his bank job. (नौकरी छोड़ दी)

◦ Correct: ... last year he left his job at the bank and is now running a tool business.

• The context word "last year" also demands a past-tense verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bereft" is an adjective meaning deprived of / lacking (bereft of hope); it cannot take a direct object like "his job".

• Option 3 "halted" means stopped temporarily — one halts a train or a process, not a job.

• Option 4 "cleft" means split or divided (a cleft chin, cleft palate) and makes no sense here.

NOTE

• Forms: leave – left – left. Common collocations: leave a job / quit a job / resign from a job / step down from a post. Do not confuse "leave" (छोड़ना) with "live" (रहना).

question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

Work in this office is done in the _________ way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. least efficient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is preceded by the definite article "the" and followed by the noun "way". The definite article "the" before a degree word signals the superlative degree.

• The descending degrees of "efficient" are: little efficient (positive) – less efficient (comparative) – least efficient (superlative). The superlative form is "least efficient".

◦ Correct: Work in this office is done in the least efficient way.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "little efficient" is the positive degree and cannot follow "the ... way" in a comparison of this kind.

• Option 2 "lesser efficient way" repeats the noun "way" (the sentence already ends with "way") and "lesser" is not used with adjectives.

• Option 3 "less efficient" is a comparative and needs "than" (less efficient than ...), which is absent here.

NOTE

• Ascending scale: efficient – more efficient – most efficient. Descending scale: efficient – less efficient – least efficient. Remember: "the" + superlative (the best, the most useful, the least efficient); comparative + "than".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The chef's delicious recipies are a favourite among the restaurant's patrons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Recipies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Recipies" is misspelt. The correct plural of *recipe* is "recipes" — a recipe is a set of instructions for preparing a dish. (व्यंजन विधि)

◦ Correct: The chef's delicious recipes are a favourite among the restaurant's patrons.

• Spelling key: RE + CI + PE, and the plural simply adds "-s" → recipes (the word does not end in a consonant + y, so there is no "y → ies" change).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Delicious" (very tasty), "chef's" (belonging to the chef) and "restaurant's" (belonging to the restaurant) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The "y → ies" rule applies only when a word ends in consonant + y: baby → babies, city → cities, story → stories. Words ending in a vowel + y or in "-e" simply add "-s": key → keys, recipe → recipes, boy → boys.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

I graciously welcomed my boss at my birthday party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nicely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Graciously" means in a kind, polite, courteous and pleasant manner. Its closest synonym among the options is "nicely" (in a pleasant, agreeable way). (शालीनता से / कृपापूर्वक)

◦ Example: She graciously/nicely accepted the invitation and thanked the host.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bravely" and Option 3 "Courageously" both relate to courage in the face of danger, not to politeness.

• Option 2 "Cleverly" means in an intelligent or shrewd way, which is unrelated to warmth or courtesy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of graciously: kindly, politely, courteously, cordially, affably, benevolently. Antonyms: rudely, ungraciously, curtly, discourteously. Related words: gracious (adjective), grace/graciousness (nouns).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Futile
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Useless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Futile" means producing no result; pointless, fruitless or ineffective. Its closest synonym is "useless". (व्यर्थ / निष्फल)

◦ Example: All their futile/useless attempts to revive the loss-making company finally ended in its closure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vicious" means cruel, violent or savage — a completely different idea.

• Option 2 "Adequate" means sufficient or enough, which is nearly the opposite of "of no use".

• Option 4 "Thoughtful" means considerate or reflective, and is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of futile: useless, vain, fruitless, pointless, unproductive, ineffectual, in vain. Antonyms: useful, fruitful, effective, productive, worthwhile. Noun form: futility (व्यर्थता).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I have lived with my parents / in Mumbai / in a residential flat / yet two years.
option_3: I have lived with my parents
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. yet two years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the present perfect ("have lived") with a period/duration of time ("two years"). With a duration, the correct preposition is "for", not the adverb "yet".

◦ Correct: I have lived with my parents in Mumbai in a residential flat for two years.

• "Yet" is used with the present perfect only in negatives and questions meaning "up to now" — "He has not come yet", "Have you eaten yet?" — never before a period of time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "I have lived with my parents" is a correct present perfect structure showing an action continuing up to the present.

• "in Mumbai" (preposition of place for a large city) and "in a residential flat" are both correct.

NOTE

• Present perfect prepositions: use "for" with a period (for two years, for six months, for a long time) and "since" with a point of time (since 2020, since Monday, since morning). "Still / yet / already" have their own fixed positions and uses.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Many fraud companies _____ (deceive) innocent customers and earn millions of dollars.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mislead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deceive" means to make someone believe something that is not true; to cheat or trick. Its closest synonym here is "mislead", which means to give a wrong idea or impression, leading someone into error. (गुमराह करना / धोखा देना)

◦ Correct: Many fraud companies mislead innocent customers and earn millions of dollars.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hamper" means to hinder or obstruct progress — it does not carry the sense of trickery.

• Option 2 "facilitate" means to make something easier — the exact opposite of harming customers.

• Option 4 "resolve" means to settle or solve a problem, which does not fit "fraud companies".

NOTE

• Synonyms of deceive: mislead, dupe, cheat, defraud, hoodwink, delude, swindle. Antonyms: enlighten, undeceive, guide. Forms: deceive (verb) – deception/deceit (nouns) – deceptive/deceitful (adjectives).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We have perhaps never seen an ablest series of advocates than these ten standing in a row.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. abler.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains "than", and "than" is always used with the comparative degree, never with the superlative. The comparative of "able" is "abler".

◦ Correct: We have perhaps never seen an abler series of advocates than these ten standing in a row.

• The article "an" already in the sentence also fits "an abler" (the vowel sound /eɪ/), confirming this option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more able" is comparative in sense, but "an more able" is grammatically wrong — "able" is a short adjective that takes "-er", and the article "an" cannot precede "more".

• Option 3 "the ablest" is a superlative and cannot be used with "than"; besides, "an the ablest" is impossible.

• Option 4 "most ablest" is a double superlative — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "able": able – abler / more able – ablest / most able. Never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est" (double comparatives/superlatives such as "more better", "most ablest", "more wiser" are grammatically wrong).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

To his surprise, it swung back at his touch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Shock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Surprise" means a feeling of astonishment caused by something sudden or unexpected. Among the options, "shock" is the closest synonym, as it too denotes a sudden, unexpected emotional jolt. (आश्चर्य / अचंभा)

◦ Example: To his surprise/shock, the heavy gate swung open at the slightest touch.

• The phrase "to one's surprise" is a fixed expression meaning "surprisingly for that person".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anger" (a feeling of rage) and Option 2 "Regret" (a feeling of sorrow over something done) are different emotions altogether.

• Option 4 "Boredom" (a feeling of weariness from dullness) is unrelated and, in fact, the opposite of a startling reaction.

NOTE

• Synonyms of surprise: astonishment, amazement, shock, wonder, bewilderment, startlement. Antonyms: expectation, anticipation, composure. Related expressions: "take by surprise", "to my surprise", "a surprise element".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Ephemeral
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Transient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time; short-lived and fleeting. Its exact synonym is "transient" (passing quickly, temporary). (क्षणभंगुर / अल्पकालिक)

◦ Example: Fame on social media is often ephemeral/transient — it fades within days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Permanent" (lasting for ever) is the antonym of ephemeral — a classic trap option.

• Option 1 "Ugly" (unpleasant to look at) and Option 3 "Pleasing" (giving pleasure) have nothing to do with duration of time.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ephemeral: transient, transitory, fleeting, momentary, short-lived, evanescent, temporary. Antonyms: permanent, everlasting, enduring, eternal, perpetual. The word comes from Greek *ephemeros* = "lasting only a day".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. and an hyena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the initial sound of the following word, not on its spelling. In "hyena", the letter h is clearly pronounced (/haɪˈiːnə/), i.e., it begins with a consonant sound, so it must take "a", not "an".

◦ Correct: A fox and a hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A fox" is correct — "fox" begins with the consonant sound /f/.

• Option 2 "were spotted in" is correct — the subject "A fox and a hyena" is plural, so the plural verb "were" is right, and the passive "were spotted" fits the sense.

• Option 4 "the animal reserve" correctly uses "the" for a specific, identified place.

NOTE

• Silent-h words take "an": an hour, an honest man, an heir, an honour. Pronounced-h words take "a": a hyena, a hotel, a horse, a history book, a habit. Similarly, "a university / a European / a one-eyed man" (consonant sounds) but "an MLA / an X-ray / an umbrella" (vowel sounds).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: She always cuts out unhealthy snacks.
option_2: The manager cuts the discussion to address an urgent matter.
option_3: Can you cut through the traffic to get here on time?
option_4: They need to cut down the old tree in the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The manager cuts the discussion to address an urgent matter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended meaning is that the manager ended the discussion earlier than planned, and the correct phrasal verb for that is "cut short", not the bare verb "cut". The sentence also needs a past tense to match the completed action.

◦ Correct: The manager cut short the discussion to address an urgent matter.

• "Cut" used alone with "the discussion" is unidiomatic in standard English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct: "cut out" = to stop consuming or doing something (She always cuts out unhealthy snacks).

• Option 3 is correct: "cut through" = to pass or move through something (Can you cut through the traffic ...?).

• Option 4 is correct: "cut down" = to fell a tree, or to reduce something (They need to cut down the old tree).

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "cut": cut off (disconnect/isolate), cut in (interrupt), cut back (reduce spending), cut down (fell/reduce), cut out (stop/remove), cut short (end prematurely), cut across (take a shortcut / go beyond boundaries).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The questions in part B looks difficult than the questions in part A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. more difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The presence of "than" in the sentence demands the comparative degree. "Difficult" is a three-syllable (long) adjective, so its comparative is formed with "more" — "more difficult".

◦ Correct: The questions in part B look more difficult than the questions in part A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "difficultier" is not a word — long adjectives never take the "-er" ending.

• Option 2 "difficultly" is an adverb form and cannot be compared with "than" here.

• Option 4 "most difficult" is the superlative, which is used with "the" and among three or more, never with "than".

NOTE

• Adjectives of one syllable (and some two-syllable ones) take -er/-est: tall–taller–tallest, easy–easier–easiest. Adjectives of three or more syllables take more/most: difficult – more difficult – most difficult; beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb.

Bite the bullet
option_1: To be the first to attack someone
option_2: To take the blame for something one didn't do
option_3: To buy something with no prior inspection
option_4: To face up to trouble with fortitude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To face up to trouble with fortitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bite the bullet" means to accept and endure something painful or unpleasant with courage; to face a difficult situation bravely because it cannot be avoided. (कठिनाई का साहस से सामना करना)

◦ Example: With no other option left, he decided to bite the bullet and pay off the entire loan at once.

• The expression comes from the days before anaesthesia, when wounded soldiers were made to bite on a bullet to bear the pain of surgery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to be the first to attack someone" is not the sense of the idiom at all.

• Option 2 "to take the blame for something one didn't do" corresponds to "take the rap / carry the can / be a scapegoat".

• Option 3 "to buy something with no prior inspection" corresponds to "buy a pig in a poke".

NOTE

• Related idioms of endurance and courage: "grin and bear it", "face the music" (accept the consequences), "take the bull by the horns" (tackle a difficulty head-on), "keep a stiff upper lip".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The student received an __________ for his outstanding performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. accolade.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accolade" is the only correctly spelt option. It means an award, honour or expression of praise given for outstanding achievement. (प्रशंसा / सम्मान)

◦ Correct: The student received an accolade for his outstanding performance.

• Spelling key: AC + CO + LADE — note the double "c" and the ending "-ade".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accolad", Option 2 "acolade" and Option 4 "acolayd" are all misspellings of the same word and have no meaning in English.

• The article "an" before the blank also confirms a word beginning with a vowel sound — "an accolade".

NOTE

• Synonyms of accolade: award, honour, tribute, commendation, praise, laurels, kudos. Historically, an accolade was the ceremonial touch on the shoulder with a sword when a person was knighted.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The soldiers are all on their toes and anxiously waiting for the orders to start marching towards the enemy.
option_2: all on their toes and anxiously dancing
option_3: all on their fingers and anxiously waiting
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment already contains the correct idiom "on one's toes", which means alert, ready and prepared for action. It fits perfectly with soldiers waiting for the order to march. (सतर्क / तैयार रहना)

◦ Correct (unchanged): The soldiers are all on their toes and anxiously waiting for the orders to start marching towards the enemy.

• Since the sentence is grammatically and idiomatically sound, no substitution is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 replaces "waiting" with "dancing", which destroys the meaning — soldiers awaiting orders are not dancing.

• Option 3 "on their fingers" is not an idiom in English; the correct body part in this idiom is "toes".

• Option 4 "paying through the nose" is a different idiom altogether, meaning to pay an excessively high price.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "keep someone on their toes" (keep them alert), "on the ball" (alert and competent), "on the alert", "wide awake". Contrast: "caught napping / off guard" (unprepared).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

We have pledged our allegance to the nation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. allegiance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "allegance" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "allegiance", which means loyalty, faithfulness or devotion to a person, country or cause. (निष्ठा / राजभक्ति)

◦ Correct: We have pledged our allegiance to the nation.

• Spelling key: AL + LE + GI + ANCE — note the double "l" and the "gi" before "-ance".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "allegaince" reverses the letters "ia" to "ai" — incorrect.

• Option 3 "alegiance" drops one "l" — incorrect.

• Option 4 "ellegance" is a distorted form of "elegance", which means grace or refined beauty — a completely different word.

NOTE

• Synonyms of allegiance: loyalty, fidelity, faithfulness, devotion, obedience. Antonyms: disloyalty, treachery, betrayal. Common collocation: "pledge/swear allegiance to" a flag, a nation or a leader.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. inhabit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inhabit" means to live in or occupy a place as one's natural home. Blue whales live throughout the vast oceans, so they "inhabit vast oceanic expanses". (निवास करना)

◦ Correct: Blue whales are the world's largest living things and inhabit vast oceanic expanses.

• Note the grammar too: "inhabit" is a transitive verb used without a preposition — inhabit a place (not "inhabit in a place").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "employ" means to hire someone for work or to make use of something — meaningless with "oceanic expanses".

• Option 2 "depart" means to leave, which contradicts the idea of living in the ocean.

• Option 4 "engage" means to occupy someone's attention or to hire, and would require "engage in/with".

NOTE

• Synonyms of inhabit: occupy, dwell in, populate, reside in, live in. Related words: inhabitant (a resident), inhabited (lived in), uninhabited (with no people living there), habitat (the natural home of an organism).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. weighs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "more than 190 metric tons", which is a measure of weight. The verb that takes a weight as its complement is "weighs" (to have a particular weight). (वज़न होना)

◦ Correct: The adult is more than 100 feet long and weighs more than 190 metric tons.

• The sentence pairs length ("more than 100 feet long") with weight ("weighs more than 190 metric tons"), giving a balanced description of the animal's size.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lifts" would mean the whale raises a 190-ton load, which is not the intended meaning.

• Option 3 "counts" refers to numbering items, not to mass.

• Option 4 "loads" means to fill or pile something onto a vehicle, which does not fit.

NOTE

• "Weigh" has two uses: intransitive — "The parcel weighs 5 kg" (it has that weight); transitive — "She weighed the parcel" (she measured its weight). Static point: the blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. intact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Intact" means complete and undamaged; kept whole with nothing removed. The bristles (baleen plates) let the water out while holding the food back, i.e., keeping their food "intact". (अक्षुण्ण / ज्यों का त्यों)

◦ Correct: Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food intact.

• The structure "keep + object + adjective" ("keep their food intact") also demands an adjective, and only "intact" is an adjective among the options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "beckon" is a verb meaning to signal someone to come — grammatically and contextually wrong.

• Option 2 "brokerage" is a noun meaning a commission or an agent's business.

• Option 3 "fair" means just/reasonable or light-coloured, and gives no sensible meaning with "keeping their food".

NOTE

• Synonyms of intact: whole, entire, undamaged, unbroken, complete, unimpaired. Antonyms: damaged, broken, impaired. Structures: keep something intact / safe / warm / clean (keep + object + adjective).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. communicate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists "whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs" as "the means by which the whales _____ with one another" — these are all forms of exchanging messages, so the verb is "communicate". (संवाद करना / संदेश आदान-प्रदान करना)

◦ Correct: ... are the means by which the whales communicate with one another.

• The collocation "communicate with" someone is exactly the structure the sentence requires, and the next line ("It assists them in locating one another ... searching for prey, and attracting mates") confirms the purpose of communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "meet" would need no "means of sounds" and does not explain the listed purposes.

• Option 2 "horrid" is an adjective meaning very unpleasant, so it cannot be the verb of the clause.

• Option 3 "catch" means to seize or grab, which does not go with "with one another" in this sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of communicate: convey, transmit, correspond, interact, converse. Related nouns: communication, communicator. Static point: whales use low-frequency sound that travels hundreds of kilometres underwater; dolphins and bats use echolocation.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. across.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Across" is a preposition meaning from one side to the other of a wide area; spanning an expanse. The whales' songs travel over an enormous stretch of sea, so they can be heard "across miles of ocean". (के पार / फैलाव में)

◦ Correct: These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days across miles of ocean.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "beside" means next to / by the side of, which cannot describe sound travelling over a huge distance.

• Option 3 "although" is a conjunction of contrast, not a preposition, so it cannot precede the noun phrase "miles of ocean".

• Option 4 "off" means away from or at a distance from, and does not convey spanning a wide area.

NOTE

• Prepositions of movement/extent: across (from one side to the other — across the river), through (from end to end inside — through the tunnel), along (following the length — along the road), over (above/covering — over the bridge).

question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulakesin II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harshavardhana's ambition of extending his empire into the Deccan and South India was checked by the Chalukya ruler Pulakesin II, who defeated him on the banks of the river Narmada (around 618–619 CE). (हर्षवर्धन को पुलकेशिन द्वितीय ने रोका)

• After this defeat, the Narmada became the southern boundary of Harsha's empire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti/Vardhana dynasty ruled from Thanesar and later Kannauj. The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited his court, and the court poet Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita.

• Pulakesin II (610–642 CE) belonged to the Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi). His victory over Harsha is recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by his court poet Ravikirti.

• Pulakesin II was later defeated and killed by the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I of Kanchi.

NOTE

• Rajaraja I was the great Chola ruler (985–1014 CE) who built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur. Ashoka was the Mauryan emperor (3rd century BCE) — both belong to entirely different periods.

question: When was India’s first ever budget presented?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1860.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first ever budget was presented on 7 April 1860 by James Wilson, the first Finance Member of the India Council under the British Crown. (भारत का पहला बजट — 1860)

• It was introduced after the Revolt of 1857, to repair the finances of the government; Wilson also introduced income tax in India in the same budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• James Wilson was also the founder of *The Economist* magazine and of the Chartered Bank (later Standard Chartered).

• The first budget of independent India was presented on 26 November 1947 by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty.

• The first budget of the Republic of India was presented by John Mathai in 1950.

NOTE

• Morarji Desai presented the maximum number of budgets (10). Indira Gandhi was the first woman to present a budget (1970), and Nirmala Sitharaman is the first full-time woman Finance Minister to do so (from 2019). The budget timing was shifted from 5 p.m. to 11 a.m. in 2001, and the Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

question: The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is zone of exclusion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clear region of cytoplasm surrounding the Golgi complex (Golgi apparatus), which is free of ribosomes and other cell organelles, is called the "zone of exclusion" (also known as the Golgi ground substance). (गोल्जी काय के चारों ओर का स्वच्छ क्षेत्र — ज़ोन ऑफ़ एक्सक्लूज़न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Camillo Golgi (1898). It consists of flattened sacs (cisternae), tubules and vesicles.

• Functions of the Golgi body: packaging, processing and dispatch of proteins and lipids, formation of lysosomes, and synthesis of cell wall material in plants. It is called the "post office of the cell" or the "traffic police of the cell".

NOTE

• Cytosol is the fluid part of the cytoplasm; cytosine is a nitrogenous base of DNA/RNA (a pyrimidine); cytochrome is a haem-containing protein of the electron transport chain in mitochondria. None of these describes a region around the Golgi body.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture?

i. Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial.

ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddh

iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and ii.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, statements i and ii are correct while statement iii is incorrect.

◦ Statement i is correct — an "Uddeshika (Uddesika) stupa" is a commemorative/memorial stupa, built to mark an event or to commemorate the Buddha and his disciples. (स्मारक स्तूप)

◦ Statement ii is accepted as correct in the key — the "Paribhogika stupa" is the second recognised category of stupa in this classification.

◦ Statement iii is incorrect — the Bharhut stupa is situated in Madhya Pradesh (Satna district), not in Uttar Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Traditional classification of stupas: Saririka (containing the bodily relics of the Buddha or saints), Paribhogika (containing objects used by the Buddha, such as his bowl or robe) and Uddeshika (commemorative, built at sacred spots).

• The Bharhut Stupa (2nd century BCE, Shunga period) is famous for its carved railings and torana, now preserved largely in the Indian Museum, Kolkata. It was discovered by Alexander Cunningham in 1873.

• The Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh), originally built by Ashoka, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Key elements of a stupa: Anda (hemispherical dome), Harmika (railing on top), Yashti (central mast), Chhatra (umbrella), Medhi (drum/base) and Pradakshina Patha (circumambulatory path).

question: If an Indian citizen is denied entry to a public place because of his caste, which of the following Fundamental Rights is denied to him?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to equality.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Denying a citizen entry to a public place on the ground of caste violates the "Right to Equality" guaranteed under Articles 14–18 of the Constitution. (समानता का अधिकार)

• Specifically, Article 15(2) states that no citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, be subjected to any disability regarding access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

• Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

• Article 16 — equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

• Article 17 — abolition of untouchability.

• Article 18 — abolition of titles.

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12–35): Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30) and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). The Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

question: ‘Ram Navami’ is celebrated in India to commemorate the:
option_2: coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
option_3: return of Lord Rama from forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is birth of Lord Rama.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ram Navami" is celebrated to commemorate the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh incarnation (avatar) of Lord Vishnu. (राम नवमी — भगवान राम का जन्मोत्सव)

• It falls on the ninth day (Navami) of the Shukla Paksha in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April) and marks the last day of Chaitra Navratri.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord Rama was born at Ayodhya to King Dasharatha and Queen Kausalya. The Ramayana, composed by Maharishi Valmiki, narrates his life; Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.

• Ram Navami is celebrated with great fervour at Ayodhya (UP), Sitamarhi (Bihar), Rameswaram (Tamil Nadu) and Bhadrachalam (Telangana).

NOTE

• Related festivals: Dussehra/Vijayadashami marks the killing of Ravana; Deepavali marks the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile; Janmashtami marks the birth of Lord Krishna.

question: In February 2024, who took an oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champai Soren.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2024, Champai Soren took the oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand, after Hemant Soren resigned following his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate. (चंपई सोरेन — झारखंड के 12वें मुख्यमंत्री)

• He belonged to the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) at that time and is popularly called the "Tiger of Kolhan" for his role in the statehood movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda) and is the 28th state of India. Its capital is Ranchi.

• Babulal Marandi was the first Chief Minister of Jharkhand.

• Arjun Munda has also served as Chief Minister of Jharkhand and later as a Union Minister for Tribal Affairs.

NOTE

• A Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164. Jharkhand's Governor at that time was C. P. Radhakrishnan. The state's High Court is at Ranchi, and its major festivals include Sarhul, Karma and Sohrai.

question: Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 for which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Art - Playback Singing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The renowned singer Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 in the field of "Art – Playback Singing". (उदित नारायण — पद्म भूषण 2016, पार्श्व गायन)

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri in 2009.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Udit Narayan is a multiple National Film Award winner, famous for songs in films such as *Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak*, *Lagaan* and *Dil To Pagal Hai*. He was born in Nepal and raised in Bihar.

• The Padma Awards, instituted in 1954, are announced every year on Republic Day (26 January) and conferred by the President of India.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna (highest) > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. Padma Bhushan is given for "distinguished service of a high order" in any field.

question: Which river is known as ‘Langchen Khambab’ in Tibet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sutlej.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sutlej river is known as "Langchen Khambab" in Tibet, which means "flowing from the mouth of the elephant". (सतलुज — लांगचेन खंबाब)

• It rises from the Rakas Tal (Rakshastal) lake near Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass in Himachal Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab and is an antecedent river (older than the Himalayas). The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on it.

• Tibetan names of Himalayan rivers: Indus – Singi Khamban ("from the lion's mouth"); Brahmaputra – Tsangpo ("the purifier"); Karnali/Ghaghara – Tamchok Khambab.

• The five rivers of Punjab: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

NOTE

• As per the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India has full rights over the Eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan gets the Western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

question: Bal Gangadhar described ______ as a diamond of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak described Gopal Krishna Gokhale as "the Diamond of India, the Jewel of Maharashtra and the Prince of Workers". (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — भारत का हीरा)

• The tribute is famous because Tilak (an Extremist) and Gokhale (a Moderate) held opposing political views, yet Tilak praised him warmly on his death in 1915.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866–1915) was a leading Moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, its President in 1905 (Banaras session), and the founder of the Servants of India Society (1905).

• He was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhi called him his political mentor; Gokhale in turn advised Gandhi to travel across India before entering politics.

NOTE

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was called "Lokmanya" and the "Father of Indian Unrest" (by Valentine Chirol). His famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it." He started the Ganpati and Shivaji festivals and published Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English).

question: ‘The Blue Umbrella’, ‘The Cherry Tree’, ‘The Hidden Pool’ are novels written by who among the following authors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Blue Umbrella", "The Cherry Tree" and "The Hidden Pool" were written by the celebrated Indian author Ruskin Bond. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

• His writing is set largely in the hills of Uttarakhand (Mussoorie, Dehradun and Landour) and is loved for its simplicity and its portrayal of nature and childhood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other famous works of Ruskin Bond: *The Room on the Roof* (his first novel, which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957), *A Flight of Pigeons* (the basis of the film *Junoon*), *Rusty* series, *Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra* (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1992).

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

• *The Blue Umbrella* was made into a National Award-winning Hindi film by Vishal Bhardwaj.

NOTE

• Anant Pai ("Uncle Pai") created Amar Chitra Katha and Tinkle; Sudha Murthy wrote *Wise and Otherwise*, *Dollar Bahu* and *How I Taught My Grandmother to Read*; Twinkle Khanna wrote *Mrs Funnybones* and *The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad*.

question: What is the overarching programme introduced in the Union Budget, 2018-19 by Government of India, for the school education sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samagra Shiksha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Samagra Shiksha" is the overarching (integrated) programme for the school education sector announced in the Union Budget 2018-19. It treats school education holistically from pre-school to Class XII. (समग्र शिक्षा)

• It subsumed three earlier schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) and Teacher Education (TE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development). Its main outcome focus is on improving quality, equity and inclusion in school education.

• Samagra Shiksha 2.0 was aligned with the recommendations of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

NOTE

• Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 — implemented from 1 April 2010 under Article 21A (inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002) — provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years. "Rashtriya Unnat Shiksha Abhiyan" and "Sarva Vidya Abhiyan" are not the names of this programme (the higher-education scheme is RUSA — Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan).

question: Who was the highest run scorer in Men’s World Cup cricket - 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohit Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rohit Sharma was the highest run scorer of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2019, scoring 648 runs in the tournament. (रोहित शर्मा — 2019 विश्व कप के सर्वाधिक रन)

• He also became the first batsman to score five centuries in a single World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup was hosted by England and Wales. England won the title for the first time, beating New Zealand in a dramatic final at Lord's decided on boundary count after a tied Super Over.

• Kane Williamson (New Zealand) was the Player of the Tournament; Mitchell Starc (Australia) was the leading wicket-taker with 27 wickets.

NOTE

• India has won the ODI World Cup twice — 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (MS Dhoni) — and the T20 World Cup in 2007 (MS Dhoni) and 2024 (Rohit Sharma). Rohit Sharma holds the record for the highest individual ODI score — 264.

question: The approximate number of water molecules present in 9 gm of water is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.011 × 10²³.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Step 1 — Molar mass of water (H₂O) = (2 × 1) + 16 = 18 g/mol.

• Step 2 — Number of moles = given mass ÷ molar mass = 9 ÷ 18 = 0.5 mole.

• Step 3 — Number of molecules = number of moles × Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³)

◦ = 0.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²³ molecules. (जल के अणुओं की संख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Avogadro's number (N_A) = 6.022 × 10²³ is the number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions) present in one mole of any substance.

• 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 litres at STP (0 °C and 1 atm).

• The concept was named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro; the constant itself was determined later.

NOTE

• Useful formulae: Moles = mass / molar mass = number of particles / 6.022 × 10²³ = volume at STP / 22.4 L. In 9 g of water there are 0.5 mole of H₂O molecules but 1 mole of hydrogen atoms (since each molecule has 2 H atoms).

question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allan Octavian Hume.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant of the Indian Civil Service, was the founder of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885. (ए. ओ. ह्यूम — भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के संस्थापक, 1885)

• The first session of the INC was held in December 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, attended by 72 delegates, and was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A. O. Hume is also called the "Father of the Indian National Congress" and, for his work in ornithology, the "Father of Indian Ornithology".

• The INC was originally planned to be held in Poona, but was shifted to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak.

• Other early leaders: Dadabhai Naoroji (called the Grand Old Man of India, who gave the Drain of Wealth theory), Surendranath Banerjee and Pherozeshah Mehta.

NOTE

• Annie Besant became the first woman President of the INC (Calcutta, 1917) and started the Home Rule Movement (1916); Mahatma Gandhi returned to India in 1915; C. F. Andrews ("Deenabandhu") was a close associate of Gandhi — none of them founded the Congress.

question: Who among the following was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527 CE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rana Sanga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Battle of Khanwa (17 March 1527), Babur defeated Rana Sanga (Rana Sangram Singh) of Mewar. (खानवा का युद्ध, 1527 — राणा सांगा की पराजय)

• This victory destroyed Rajput resistance to Mughal expansion and firmly established Mughal rule in northern India. Babur assumed the title "Ghazi" after this battle.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Babur's key battles: First Battle of Panipat (1526) — defeated Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire; Khanwa (1527) — defeated Rana Sanga; Chanderi (1528) — defeated Medini Rai; Ghaghra (1529) — defeated the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi.

• Babur introduced the Tulughma (flanking) war tactic and the Araba (cart) formation along with gunpowder artillery in India.

NOTE

• Babur wrote his memoirs, the "Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)", in Chagatai Turkish; it was later translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan. Hasan Khan Mewati fought alongside Rana Sanga at Khanwa and was killed there.

question: Where was the inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) organised in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023 was held in Mumbai, at the Dr D. Y. Patil Sports Academy, Navi Mumbai, on 4 March 2023. (डब्ल्यूपीएल 2023 का उद्घाटन मैच — मुंबई)

• The opening match was played between the Mumbai Indians and the Gujarat Giants, and Mumbai Indians won it comfortably.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Mumbai Indians, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, won the first WPL title (2023), defeating the Delhi Capitals in the final.

• The WPL is organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and has five franchises: Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, UP Warriorz and Gujarat Giants.

• Royal Challengers Bangalore won the 2024 edition.

NOTE

• India's women's cricket milestones: Mithali Raj (highest run scorer in women's ODIs), Jhulan Goswami (highest wicket-taker in women's ODIs) and Harmanpreet Kaur (current captain). India were runners-up in the 2017 Women's ODI World Cup and the 2020 Women's T20 World Cup.

question: ‘Chakyar Koothu’, the folk dance form in which the entire story is presented by a single performer, primarily belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chakyar Koothu" is a traditional solo performing art of Kerala, in which a single performer (the Chakyar) narrates the entire story — usually episodes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas — with expressive gestures and witty social commentary. (चाक्यार कूथु — केरल)

• It is performed inside the Koothambalam (the temple theatre) and is accompanied by the Mizhavu drum and cymbals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala's other art forms: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (classical dances), Koodiyattam (the oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Ottamthullal, Theyyam, Kalaripayattu (martial art) and Chavittu Nadakam.

• Ottamthullal, created by Kunchan Nambiar, is called the "poor man's Kathakali" and is also a solo form.

NOTE

• Folk/tribal dances by state: Tripura – Hojagiri; Sikkim – Singhi Chham, Maruni; Tamil Nadu – Karagattam, Kummi, Kolattam, Therukoothu; Kerala – Chakyar Koothu, Theyyam, Thiruvathirakali.

question: Which of the following sectors had the largest percentage of workforce in urban India in the year 2019-2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Service.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In urban India during 2019-2020, the largest share of the workforce was engaged in the "Service (tertiary) sector". (सेवा क्षेत्र — शहरी भारत में सर्वाधिक कार्यबल)

• Urban employment is dominated by trade, transport, communication, banking, insurance, education, health, IT and other services, whereas agriculture dominates rural employment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three sectors of the economy: Primary (agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining), Secondary (manufacturing, construction — industry) and Tertiary (services).

• The services sector contributes the largest share of India's GDP (over 50%), while agriculture still employs the largest share of the total (rural + urban) workforce in India.

• Employment data is collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

NOTE

• Important terms: Disguised unemployment (common in agriculture), seasonal unemployment, Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and the Unemployment Rate (UR) — all measured by the PLFS.

question: National Prophylaxis Program, which was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to address which of the following medical conditions /diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blindness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Prophylaxis Programme against Nutritional Blindness" was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to prevent blindness caused by Vitamin A deficiency among children. (नेत्रहीनता — विटामिन A की कमी से)

• Under the programme, massive doses of Vitamin A are administered to children aged 9 months to 5 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness, xerophthalmia, Bitot's spots and eventually total blindness. Sources: carrots, green leafy vegetables, milk, eggs and liver.

• The National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB) was launched in 1976, the world's first national programme of its kind, with the goal of reducing the prevalence of blindness.

NOTE

• Deficiency diseases: Vitamin A → night blindness; Vitamin B1 (thiamine) → beriberi; Vitamin B3 → pellagra; Vitamin C → scurvy; Vitamin D → rickets/osteomalacia; Iodine → goitre; Iron → anaemia. Hypercalcemia is an *excess* of calcium, not a deficiency disease.

question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 163.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 163 of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at its head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except where he is required to act in his discretion. (अनुच्छेद 163)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 153 — there shall be a Governor for each State.

• Article 154 — the executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.

• Article 155 — the Governor is appointed by the President.

• Article 156 — the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (normal term 5 years).

• Article 157 — qualifications for appointment as Governor (must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age).

• Article 164 — appointment of the Chief Minister and other Ministers by the Governor; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

• Article 167 — duties of the Chief Minister regarding furnishing of information to the Governor.

NOTE

• The corresponding provision at the Centre is Article 74 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President) — made binding on the President by the 42nd and 44th Amendments. Note that the Governor's discretionary powers are wider than the President's.

question: As per the reforms of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023, how many minerals have been removed from the list of atomic minerals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill/Act, 2023, six (6) minerals were removed from the list of atomic minerals in Part B of the First Schedule. (परमाणु खनिजों की सूची से 6 खनिज हटाए गए)

• The six minerals removed are: Beryl and other beryllium-bearing minerals; Lithium-bearing minerals; Niobium-bearing minerals; Titanium-bearing minerals and ores; Tantalum-bearing minerals; and Zirconium-bearing minerals and ores.

• Their removal allows private sector participation in the exploration and mining of these critical minerals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Amendment also introduced the concept of "exploration licence" for deep-seated and critical minerals, and empowered the Central Government to auction mining leases and composite licences for 24 critical and strategic minerals.

• These minerals are essential for electric vehicles, batteries, solar panels, semiconductors and defence and space technologies.

NOTE

• The parent legislation is the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, administered by the Ministry of Mines. The Geological Survey of India (GSI), established in 1851, is headquartered at Kolkata.

question: K Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 1999, for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1999 for his outstanding contribution to "Bharatnatyam". (के. कल्याणसुंदरम पिल्लई — भरतनाट्यम)

• He belonged to the famous Thanjavur (Tanjore) school of Bharatanatyam and headed the Sri Rajarajeshwari Bharata Natya Kala Mandir, Mumbai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra. It was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam and was revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra) and E. Krishna Iyer.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama, was established in 1952-53 and is the oldest national academy for the performing arts.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India/UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: A portion of landmass from the shore line up to the shelf break that is submerged under shallow water is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Continental Shelf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Continental Shelf" is the gently sloping, shallow, submerged extension of a continent, stretching from the shoreline up to the shelf break (where the slope suddenly steepens). (महाद्वीपीय मग्नतट)

• Its average depth is about 100–200 metres and the average gradient is less than 1°.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The continental shelf is the richest fishing ground in the world because sunlight penetrates the shallow water, supporting plankton growth. It is also a major source of petroleum and natural gas (e.g., Bombay High).

• Order of ocean relief features from the coast: Continental Shelf → Continental Slope → Continental Rise → Abyssal Plain (Deep Sea Plain) → Ocean Deeps/Trenches.

• Trenches are the deepest parts of the ocean — the Mariana Trench in the Pacific (Challenger Deep) is the deepest point on Earth.

NOTE

• Under UNCLOS, a coastal state's Territorial Sea extends 12 nautical miles and its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) up to 200 nautical miles. Continental Drift Theory was proposed by Alfred Wegener (1912) — it is a theory, not a relief feature.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in the three main dimensions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991, announced by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Urbanisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 (the New Economic Policy) rested on three main dimensions — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG). "Urbanisation" is NOT one of them. (एलपीजी — उदारीकरण, निजीकरण, वैश्वीकरण)

◦ Liberalisation — removal of licensing, quotas and unnecessary government controls on business.

◦ Privatisation — reducing the role of the public sector and inviting private ownership/disinvestment.

◦ Globalisation — integrating the Indian economy with the world economy through trade and investment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The reforms were announced on 24 July 1991 under Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, in response to the Balance of Payments crisis of 1991.

• Key measures: abolition of industrial licensing for most industries (retained for a few), reduction of the number of industries reserved for the public sector from 17 to 8 (later to 3, now 2), MRTP Act relaxation, and liberal FDI norms.

NOTE

• Earlier industrial policies: 1948 (first Industrial Policy Resolution), 1956 (the "Economic Constitution of India", classifying industries into Schedules A, B and C), 1977, 1980 and 1991. Urbanisation is a demographic process, not an economic-reform dimension.
